segments: Today we're going to talk about something that really happened at school.
I'll go first and then it'll be your turn.
Last week I sang in a choir concert because my friend asked me to join.
I forgot one line, but nobody noticed, and I felt relieved.
You were summer with a sun hat.
How did you feel before you went on?
Nervous, with lots of mums and dads watching.
I said my line, so everyone clapped.
You said your line, so everyone clapped.
How did that make you feel?
And how did the assembly finish?
Let me say your story back to you.
Your class did an assembly in the hall with Miss Hart.
It was a play about the seasons, and you were summer with a sun hat.
You felt nervous because lots of mums and dads were watching, then you said your line, so everyone clapped, and you felt proud.
Thanks for telling me your story.
You did a really great job.

Therapist. An assembly. Who was in it? Child. My class. And Miss Hart. Therapist. Your class and Miss Hart. Where was it? Child. In the hall. Therapist. In the hall. What happened? Child. We did a play. About the seasons. Therapist. A play about the seasons. What did you do? Child. I was summer. I had a sun hat. Therapist. You were summer with a sun hat. How did you feel before you went on? Child. Nervous. Lots of mums and dads. Therapist. Nervous, with lots of mums and dads watching. What happened next? Child. I said my line, so everyone clapped. Therapist. You said your line, so everyone clapped. How did that make you feel? Child. Proud. Therapist. Proud. You must have been delighted. And how did the assembly finish? Child. Can't remember. Therapist. That's okay. Let me say your story back to you. Your class did an assembly in the hall with Miss Hart. It was a play about the seasons, and you were summer with a sun hat. You felt nervous because lots of mums and dads were watching, then you said your line, so everyone clapped, and you felt proud. Did I get that right? Child. Yeah. Therapist. Thanks for telling me your story. You did a really great job.
